page.description: MikroTik RouterOS 7.25 editions and architectures: compare CHR virtual images and the x86 install ISO, download official images, or prepare a USB with ROMinit CLI.
page.intro: MikroTik's Linux-based router OS, shipped on its own RouterBOARD hardware and installable on a PC (x86) or as a virtual machine image (CHR).
pros: One OS for routing, firewall, VPN, hotspot and wireless, configured from WinBox, WebFig or the CLI.
The x86 ISO turns an ordinary PC into a router; CHR images cover VMware, VirtualBox, Hyper-V and Proxmox.
The publisher publishes CHR images in five hypervisor formats, not just a raw disk.
Devices keep receiving updates for as long as their RAM allows, including long-discontinued models.
cons: Proprietary: x86 and CHR installs run a 24-hour free trial and then need a licence key.
MikroTik publishes no checksum file for these images, so the SHA-256 values here were computed by ROMinit.
The download page is a JavaScript app; version discovery has to go through the update channel or the file host.
SwOS, the OS on MikroTik switches, is a separate product: this record covers RouterOS only.
page.previewNote: No screenshot with a reusable licence was confirmed for RouterOS; the page shows the logo only. No image was written to a USB stick and nothing was booted.
page.status: For x86, write the ISO to a USB stick with dd or Rufus, boot it and press "i" to install onto the machine's disk. For CHR, attach the disk image to a virtual machine and boot it. Both installs start on a 24-hour trial and need a licence key afterwards.

editions.name: x86 install ISO
editions.description: Bootable installer for a PC: RouterOS is written to the machine's own disk.
editions.usbNote: 68 MB image. The publisher documents writing it to a USB stick with dd or Rufus and booting from it.

editions.name: CHR virtual images
editions.description: Cloud Hosted Router disk images for hypervisors; CHR runs on x86_64 virtual machines.
editions.usbNote: 44 MB archive per format. These are virtual disk images for hypervisors, not images for writing to a USB stick.

requirements.summary: 64 MB RAM · 64 MB storage · supported NIC
requirements.note: x86 installs need an x86 or ARM CPU, a storage medium and network cards the Linux kernel supports. CHR runs on x86_64 virtual machines with 256 MB RAM and 128 MB disk at the minimum.
